issues.description: The problem statement's task text specifies addGuestStudents(String) but the UML diagram and the solution implementation use addGuestStudents(int): this mismatch of the parameter type (String vs int) can confuse students about which signature to implement and will cause tests or reference solution code to disagree with the written instruction.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the problem statement with the UML and solution by changing the task text to require addGuestStudents(int). Update the task description line that currently reads addGuestStudents(String) to addGuestStudents(int) (or alternatively modify the UML and solution to accept a String, but using int is recommended since guest student counts are numeric).

issues.description: The problem statement text (line specifying the method signature) refers to addGuestStudents(String) while the UML diagram and both template/solution code expect addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch between the described method signature in the problem text and the implementation/UML creates confusion about the expected parameter type for the same conceptual operation (adding guest students). Students could implement the wrong signature or be uncertain whether to accept a String or an int.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the problem statement with the UML and code by changing the method signature in the problem text to addGuestStudents(int). Alternatively, update the UML and solution to accept a String if the intent is to pass numeric values as Strings — but prefer using int for numeric guest counts to avoid unnecessary parsing for students.
